![](/images/uq1.jpg){width="100%"}

Each tool is a self-contained Jupyter notebook that runs in your browser — no installation of R or any other software is required. Simply click a launch button below, wait for the environment to load (this may take a minute or two), and start working with your own texts.

```{=html}
<div class="launch-info">
  <div class="launch-option recommended">
    <div class="lo-label">⭐ Recommended</div>

Requires authentication through an Australian or New Zealand research organisation covered by the <a href="https://aaf.edu.au/">AAF</a> or <a href="https://www.reannz.co.nz/products-and-services/tuakiri">Tuakiri</a>.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="launch-option open">

    <p>Free and open — no account or institutional login required. Suitable for users outside Australia/New Zealand or without AAF/Tuakiri access. May have lower resource limits.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Concordancing {#concordancing}

```{=html}
<div class="tool-card">
  <div class="tool-card-header">
    <div class="tool-icon">🔍</div>
    <div class="tool-card-header-text">
      <h3>Concordancing Tool</h3>
      <p>Extract KWIC displays and download the results as a table</p>
    </div>
    <span class="tool-input-badge">Input: plain text file(s)</span>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card-body">
    <p>The Concordancing Tool creates <strong>K</strong>ey<strong>w</strong>ord-<strong>i</strong>n-<strong>C</strong>ontext (KWIC) displays of words or phrases across a single text or collection of texts, and allows you to download the resulting table. Use it to examine how a chosen word or phrase is used in context, to compare usage across texts, or to build evidence for a discourse analysis.</p>
    <a href="/tutorials/kwics/kwics.html" class="tool-learn-link">→ Learn more: Concordancing Tutorial</a>
    <div class="launch-buttons">
      <a href="https://binderhub.rc.nectar.org.au/v2/gh/SLCLADAL/interactive-notebooks-environment/main?urlpath=git-pull%3Frepo%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fgithub.com%252FSLCLADAL%252Finteractive-notebooks%26urlpath%3Dlab%252Ftree%252Finteractive-notebooks%252Fnotebooks%252Fkwictool.ipynb%26branch%3Dmain" class="launch-btn ardc">
        <span class="launch-btn-icon">🚀</span>
        <span class="launch-btn-text">
          <span class="lbt-title">Launch on ARDC BinderHub</span>
          <span class="lbt-sub">Requires AAF / Tuakiri login</span>
        </span>
        <span class="rec-tag">Recommended</span>
```

## Collocations {#collocations}

```{=html}
<div class="tool-card">
  <div class="tool-card-header c2">
    <div class="tool-icon">🔗</div>
    <div class="tool-card-header-text">
      <h3>Collocation Tool</h3>
      <p>Calculate association measures and download the results</p>
    </div>
    <span class="tool-input-badge">Input: plain text file(s)</span>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card-body">
    <p>The Collocation Tool calculates association measures (collocation statistics) based on your text input and allows you to download the resulting table. Association measures quantify which words are statistically more likely to occur near each other — helping you identify significant phraseological patterns, multi-word expressions, and lexical tendencies in your texts.</p>
    <a href="/tutorials/coll/coll.html" class="tool-learn-link">→ Learn more: Collocation and N-gram Analysis Tutorial</a>
```

## Keywords {#keywords}

```{=html}
<div class="tool-card">
  <div class="tool-card-header c3">
    <div class="tool-icon">🔑</div>
    <div class="tool-card-header-text">
      <h3>Keyword Tool</h3>
      <p>Identify vocabulary distinctive to your texts relative to a reference corpus</p>
    </div>
    <span class="tool-input-badge">Input: texts + reference corpus</span>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card-body">
    <p>The Keyword Tool calculates keyness measures describing how words are over- or under-represented in your texts compared to a reference corpus. This is useful for identifying vocabulary that is distinctive to a particular text, author, genre, or time period — and for contrastive corpus analysis more generally.</p>
    <a href="/tutorials/key/key.html" class="tool-learn-link">→ Learn more: Keyness and Keyword Analysis Tutorial</a>
```

## Part-of-Speech Tagging {#pos-tagging}

```{=html}
<div class="tool-card">
  <div class="tool-card-header c4">
    <div class="tool-icon">🏷️</div>
    <div class="tool-card-header-text">
      <h3>POS Tagging Tool</h3>
      <p>Add part-of-speech tags to texts in 60+ languages</p>
    </div>
    <span class="tool-input-badge">Input: plain text file(s)</span>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card-body">
    <p>The POS Tagging Tool adds <strong>p</strong>art-<strong>o</strong>f-<strong>s</strong>peech tags to your texts in more than 60 languages, and allows you to download the tagged output. POS tagging can isolate specific word classes (e.g. all nouns across a corpus), disambiguate words that can function as more than one part of speech, or serve as a pre-processing step for more advanced grammatical analysis.</p>
    <a href="/tutorials/llr/llr.html" class="tool-learn-link">→ Learn more: Analysing Learner Language Tutorial</a>
    <div class="launch-buttons">
```

## Corpus Text Cleaning {#corpus-text-cleaning}

```{=html}

      <p>Remove and replace words, tags, and patterns across your texts</p>
    </div>

  </div>

    <p>The Corpus Cleaning Tool allows you to remove and replace words, tags, and other elements from uploaded text data, and to download the cleaned texts. ## Network Analysis {#network-analysis}
```

```{=html}
<div class="tool-card">
  <div class="tool-card-header c6">
    <div class="tool-icon">🕸️</div>
    <div class="tool-card-header-text">
      <h3>Network Analysis Tool</h3>
      <p>Generate and visualise network graphs from structured edge-list data</p>
    </div>
    <span class="tool-input-badge">Input: edge list (structured data)</span>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card-body">
    <p>The Network Analysis Tool generates and downloads network graphs from your data. Unlike the other tools, this one requires <strong>structured data describing edges (connections) and their weights</strong> rather than plain text files. Network analysis can visualise and quantify relationships between words, characters, authors, speakers, or any other entities that can be meaningfully connected.</p>
    <a href="/tutorials/net/net.html" class="tool-learn-link">→ Learn more: Network Analysis Tutorial</a>
    <div class="launch-buttons">
      <a href="https://binderhub.rc.nectar.org.au/v2/gh/SLCLADAL/interactive-notebooks-environment/main?urlpath=git-pull%3Frepo%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fgithub.com%252FSLCLADAL%252Finteractive-notebooks%26urlpath%3Dlab%252Ftree%252Finteractive-notebooks%252Fnotebooks%252Fnettool.ipynb%26branch%3Dmain" class="launch-btn ardc">
        <span class="launch-btn-icon">🚀</span>
        <span class="launch-btn-text">
          <span class="lbt-title">Launch on ARDC BinderHub</span>
          <span class="lbt-sub">Requires AAF / Tuakiri login</span>
        </span>
```

## Sentiment Analysis {#sentiment-analysis}

```{=html}

    </div>
    <span class="tool-input-badge">Input: plain text file(s)</span>
  </div>

    <p>The Sentiment Analysis Tool performs word-level sentiment scoring to estimate whether texts lean positive or negative, and downloads the results as an Excel spreadsheet. It can also examine eight basic emotional associations — <strong>anger, fear, anticipation, trust, surprise, sadness, joy,</strong> and <strong>disgust</strong> — of the words in your texts, providing a richer picture of emotional tone across a corpus.</p>
```
